haiku-low.q1: It does not differ. Both return HTTP 401 and the login page showing "Invalid email or password".
haiku-low.q2: It gets HTTP 429 with Retry-After for 15 minutes, and the password is not checked. No failure is recorded during the lock.
haiku-low.q3: On successful login, the existing session row for that cookie is deleted, whichever user owns it. A failed login leaves the existing session unchanged.
haiku-low.q4: Only the opaque 43-character session ID, named sid. It is flagged HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax. No user data is in the cookie.
haiku-low.q5: At 12 hours after login. The absolute expiry is never extended, so continuous use still ends it then. The 30-minute idle limit does not apply while requests keep coming.
haiku-low.q6: It finds zero matching rows, so it redirects with 302 to /login and sets Set-Cookie clearing sid. The login page shows no error message.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row first, then clears the cookie and redirects 302 to /login. If the session is already gone, the response is the same.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, shared by both app instances. Any instance hashes the cookie value and queries that table, so no sticky sessions are needed.
haiku-low.q9: Each failure is a row in the Postgres login_failures table with the normalized email and timestamp. Failures count if failed_at is within 10 minutes of clock_timestamp().
haiku-low.q10: It compares last_seen_at against 30 minutes ago and absolute_expires_at against now. If both hold, it sets last_seen_at to now and returns user_id.
haiku-low.q11: HTTP 503 with "We could not check your sign-in. Try again in a moment." No cookie is set, no session is created, and the transaction is rolled back.
haiku-low.q12: A cleanup job runs every 10 minutes on either instance, deleting expired sessions, old failure rows and expired lock rows. It is guarded by an advisory lock so only one instance runs it.

sonnet.q1: They don't differ: both get HTTP 401 and the login page showing "Invalid email or password". (Bcrypt is also run against a dummy hash for unknown emails so timing matches.)
sonnet.q2: It is refused with HTTP 429 (login page with the "Too many failed sign-in attempts. Try again later." message and a Retry-After in seconds), without checking the password, inserting a failure row or counting. Even a correct password gets 429. The lock lasts 15 minutes from the 5th failure.
sonnet.q3: On successful login a new random session ID is always issued, and the old session row (if the incoming sid is present and well formed, whichever user owns it) is deleted in the same transaction. If the sid is absent, duplicated or malformed, nothing is deleted. A failed login leaves the existing session unchanged.
sonnet.q4: Only the opaque 43-character random session ID (cookie name sid); no user data. Page scripts cannot read it because it is HttpOnly (also Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, host-only).
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login, the absolute limit, which is never extended. Continuous activity keeps resetting the 30-minute idle clock but not the 12-hour clock.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns zero rows, so the server clears the sid cookie (Set-Cookie with Max-Age=0) and redirects 302 to /login with no message. The page handler does not run.
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the session row from the database first, then clears the cookie and redirects 302 to /login. If the session is already gone (or there is no usable sid), it gives the same 302 with the cookie cleared; with no usable sid no database call is made. If the database errors, it returns 503 and keeps the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In Postgres (a sessions table, storing the SHA-256 hash of the session ID). Both instances share that one database, so whichever instance gets the request hashes the cookie value and looks up/updates the row by id_hash. No sticky sessions or Redis.
sonnet.q9: In a Postgres login_failures table, one row per failure with a failed_at timestamp (email normalized). Failures in the window are those rows with failed_at > clock_timestamp() - interval '10 minutes' (a sliding window, using the database clock), counted after inserting the current failure.
sonnet.q10: In a single UPDATE it compares the database clock now(): last_seen_at > now() - 30 minutes (idle) and absolute_expires_at > now() (absolute), matching on the SHA-256 of the sid. If both hold it sets last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 login page with "We could not check your sign-in. Try again in a moment." The transaction is rolled back, no cookie is set, no session is created, and the attempt is not counted.
sonnet.q12: A cleanup job running every 10 minutes on either instance (guarded by a Postgres advisory lock so only one runs at a time) deletes sessions rows where absolute_expires_at <= now() or last_seen_at <= now() - 30 minutes.
